repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgTggz8AL2bCABoDGis

Follow-up of #34987. Filed by the #34987 card thread at the seat's direction (L2 adoption 7028992664 on PR #35713). Source: contract review record 7028965301, nits N1–N5, accepted for that head and carried here. Not started (seat repo:objectstack#1 takes p1 only).

## Items
- N3 (user-facing, first) — a hook lowered from an inline `handler` gets its finding at `hooks[N].handler`, but the generic hint says "Fix body.source". Give the lowered case a hint that names the handler.
- N1 — `packages/lint/src/validate-hook-body-compiles.ts` module note says a `suppressWarnings` entry can address one rule id; that key exists on the dashboard widget only and the CLI has no per-rule suppression. Correct the note (the two-id choice stands on `os explain` and the finding's `rule` field).
- N2 — "No door publishes a job at run time" (the `reason` of semantic entry `hook-job-body-does-not-compile-refused`, and the registry comment in `authoring-rules.ts`) is true of the metadata publish door only: the boot and `os package install` bring hook and job bodies in from an artifact and run no author-time rule. Narrow the sentence to what is true.
- N4 — no run-time pin shows QuickJS refuses the two pinned bodies inside the `(ctx)` wrapper; the claim rests on the action wrapper's pin and the same grammar production. Add one runtime pin (hook and job) in the runner's tests.
- N5 — code outside PR #35713's diff still describes the hook wrapper as the AsyncFunction constructor, and the parse checker builds its own `__body(ctx)` enclosure, against the widened ⛔ line in `packages/lint/src/action-body-wrapper.ts` ("never spell the wrapper a second time anywhere"). Bring those descriptions in line, or record why the parse enclosure is a different thing.

## Reproduce
Read each named location on `main` after PR #35713 lands; N4 is the absence of a pin in `packages/runtime` tests over `hookBodyFunctionExpression`.

Not in scope: the runtime's generic `threw` sentence for a hook/job compile failure (#35715); the skills doc (#35714).

Grade: left to triage.
